idiom_name: express-rate-limit middleware (windowMs/limit over a store, standard RateLimit headers)
implementation_notes: Express has no built-in limiter, and express-rate-limit is the dominant realization: rateLimit({windowMs, limit, ...}) returns middleware that counts hits per key - IP by default, with ipv6Subnet handling - in a store and answers 429 once the limit is exceeded. The options that carry real semantics are standardHeaders ('draft-6'/'draft-7'/'draft-8' RateLimit headers), legacyHeaders, keyGenerator, skip and skipSuccessfulRequests/skipFailedRequests, and store: the built-in MemoryStore is per process, so multi-instance deployments must plug a shared store (Redis, Memcached). passOnStoreError chooses fail-open over fail-closed when the store is unreachable.
pitfalls: The default MemoryStore is per process: behind N replicas the effective limit is N times the configured one.
Wrong trust proxy / IP-resolution configuration keys all requests behind a proxy to one bucket, or to none.
skipSuccessfulRequests/skipFailedRequests change what is metered after the response completes; enabling them on an auth endpoint can invert the intent.
A failing external store either blocks all traffic or lets it through depending on passOnStoreError - the default must be chosen consciously.

variants.name: Bottleneck outbound scheduler
variants.implementation_notes: Bottleneck approaches the same problem from the client side: instead of refusing excess requests it queues them and controls when they run - minTime spaces successive jobs, maxConcurrent bounds in-flight work, and a reservoir renews a quota on an interval for services that refill a budget rather than expose a rate. Jobs enter through schedule()/wrap()/submit(), and the Redis datastore plus clustering support shares one limiter across processes. Use it to pace calls against a metered dependency; use express-rate-limit when the job is admitting inbound traffic.
variants.code_sketch:
import Bottleneck from 'bottleneck'
const limiter = new Bottleneck({ maxConcurrent: 1, minTime: 333 })  // ~3/s
const callQuotaApi = limiter.wrap(api.request)
const result = await callQuotaApi(arg)     // queued and spaced, not rejected
pitfalls: Bottleneck buffers by design: if arrival rate exceeds drain rate the queue grows unbounded unless the caller also bounds queue length.
schedule() must return a promise that resolves only after all work completes; resolving early releases the slot and breaks the pacing.
Cluster mode depends on Redis being reachable and correctly configured; a broken datastore stalls the queue or loses the shared limit.
